home.intro: I’m a backend-focused Java developer and BCA student who pairs Spring Boot, REST API, and SQL (MySQL, PostgreSQL) skills with systems-level C experience and open-source contributions to Godot Engine.
home.note: My favourite kind of learning is building something, hitting a bug, and figuring out why.

cards.title: Backend things
cards.text: Java, Spring Boot, REST APIs, MySQL & PostgreSQL, and building software that behaves well beyond the happy path.

cards.title: Under the hood
cards.text: C, processes, raw TCP sockets, memory management, file descriptors, and the details that make computers work.

facts: I’ve merged 3 bug-fix pull requests into Godot Engine 4.8 (#124054, #124170, #123035) out of 11 submitted, with 6 more under review.
I built a POSIX-compliant shell (SXSHELL) in C across 7 modules (~550 lines) with 7 built-ins, 4 redirection operators, and pipelines.
My open-source Next.js Resume Builder has earned 16 GitHub stars and 8 forks.
One of my Godot Engine regression fixes (#124170, fixing script editor tooltips) was merged 33 hours after submission.
I’m currently building a lightweight HTTP/1.1 server using raw TCP sockets in C.
I maintain an 8.84 CGPA (9.33 SGPA in Semester 3) in my BCA degree alongside Harvard CS50x and CS50 SQL certifications.
Switching between Java Spring Boot, low-level C systems code, and open-source game engine contributions gives me fresh perspectives on software design.

interests.title: Things I like learning about
interests.intro: I like understanding how a thing works, not just learning how to use it. These are the areas I keep coming back to.

items.title: Java backend development
items.description: I’m focused on how backend applications are structured, how REST APIs communicate, and how data moves reliably between an application and relational databases like MySQL and PostgreSQL using Java and Spring Boot.
items.Highlight: Focusing on clean REST API design, Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), relational data modeling, and shipping reliable server-side services.

items.title: Systems programming
items.description: Writing a POSIX shell in C made operating-system concepts feel much more concrete. I enjoy exploring process creation, file descriptors, pipes, raw TCP sockets, memory management, and what actually happens when a command runs.
items.Highlight: Building tools from scratch—like SXSHELL (7 modules, 7 built-ins, 4 redirection operators), an HTTP server, and a garbage collector—to demystify OS internals.

items.title: Open source & game development
items.description: I’m an active open-source contributor to the Godot Engine (3 merged pull requests in Godot 4.8 out of 11 submitted) and enjoy exploring game development and graphics programming in Unity and C#.
items.Highlight: Navigating large C++ engine codebases, fixing editor regressions in Godot 4.8, and prototyping gameplay systems in Unity.

projects.title: Projects and experiments
projects.intro: I learn best by making things, testing them, and figuring out the parts I don’t understand yet. Here are my open-source projects, systems tools, and backend builds.

items.title: SXSHELL — Unix-like Shell
items.description: A POSIX-compliant Unix-like shell written in C across 7 modules (~550 lines) with 7 built-ins, $PATH resolution, quote and escape parsing, 4 redirection operators, multi-command pipelines, persistent history, and $VAR expansion.
items.learning: Built to understand process creation, file descriptors, and the POSIX system calls behind terminal execution.
underTheHood: Implemented 4 redirection operators and multi-command pipelines using fork(), execv(), and dup2()
Built 7 modular C components (~550 lines) supporting 7 built-in commands, $PATH lookup, and quote/escape parsing
Added persistent history with arrow-key navigation, $VAR expansion, and architecture documentation in DOCS.md

items.title: Resume Builder
items.description: An open-source resume builder web application featuring live PDF preview and multiple customizable templates, earning 16 GitHub stars and 8 forks from the developer community.
items.learning: Focused on clean document state management, real-time PDF rendering, and shipping a polished tool used by other developers.
underTheHood: Built with TypeScript and Next.js 14 with instant live PDF preview and multi-template switching
Earned 16 GitHub stars and 8 forks through clean UX and structured resume schema state
Supports ATS-friendly formatting, section customization, and one-click PDF export

items.title: Custom HTTP Server
items.description: A lightweight HTTP server in C built over raw TCP sockets, focused on request parsing, header inspection, and HTTP response handling from the ground up.
items.learning: The goal is to master networking fundamentals by implementing the TCP socket and HTTP request-response lifecycle directly.
underTheHood: POSIX socket lifecycle: socket(), bind(), listen(), accept(), recv(), and send()
Zero-dependency HTTP request line, header parser, and status-code response builder
Static file serving with MIME type detection and client connection handling

items.title: Custom Garbage Collector
items.description: A custom garbage collector in C built to understand manual memory management, heap allocation internals, and automatic object reachability tracking.
items.learning: Explores mark-and-sweep collection, root pointer tracing, and allocation metadata at the pointer level.
underTheHood: Tracks dynamically allocated objects via an intrusive metadata header and allocation list
Mark phase traverses reachable object graphs from registered stack/root pointers
Sweep phase reclaims unmarked heap blocks and prevents memory leaks

items.title: Git Implementation in C
items.description: A simplified Git clone written in C to understand content-addressable storage, blob and tree objects, and commit history DAGs.
items.learning: Covers binary file I/O, cryptographic hashing, compression, and version control internals from scratch.
underTheHood: Implements object hashing and content-addressable storage inside .git/objects
Reads and writes blob, tree, and commit objects with header framing
Demystifies how Git snapshots file trees rather than storing simple line diffs

items.title: E-commerce Backend API
items.description: A complete e-commerce REST backend built with Spring Boot, featuring product catalog management, order workflows, JWT authentication, and pagination.
items.learning: Focused on enterprise backend architecture, relational database modeling, and clean service-layer separation.
underTheHood: Layered Spring Boot architecture (Controller → Service → Repository) with Spring Data JPA
Stateless JWT authentication, role-based access control, and request validation
PostgreSQL schema with indexed queries and paginated product endpoints

items.title: Expense Tracker API
items.description: A secure REST API for personal expense tracking, demonstrating robust CRUD operations, category analytics, Spring Security integration, and Docker containerization.
items.learning: Built to practice API security beyond the happy path, error handling, and containerized deployment.
underTheHood: Spring Security filter chain with BCrypt password hashing and user-scoped data isolation
Normalized SQL schema for transactions, recurring budgets, and monthly aggregations
Docker Compose setup bundling the Spring Boot service and PostgreSQL database

about.title: Learning by making things
about.intro: I’m Shiva Kar, a backend-focused Java developer, open-source contributor to Godot Engine, and BCA student at Amity University Online (CGPA 8.84). This page covers my open-source experience, academic background, and certifications.
approachParagraphs: I enjoy projects that force me to look beyond the surface. Building SXSHELL (a 7-module POSIX shell in C) made me think carefully about parsing input, launching processes with fork() and execv(), wiring pipelines with dup2(), and handling edge cases.
My primary professional focus is Java backend development—building and shipping REST APIs with Spring Boot, MySQL, and PostgreSQL while grounding my engineering decisions in strong CS fundamentals.

I’m also an active open-source contributor to the Godot Engine (with 3 merged bug-fix pull requests in Godot 4.8 out of 11 submitted), which has taught me how to read large codebases, collaborate with maintainers, and ship production fixes fast.
